cards.back: Time-dependent strain increase under a sustained applied stress.
Time-dependent stress decrease under a sustained imposed strain.
A dynamic protein assembly linking integrins to the actin cytoskeleton and signaling machinery.
An imaging method that estimates cell-generated forces from substrate deformation.
Conversion of mechanical cues into biochemical or gene-regulatory responses.
A perturbation showing that a component is required for an outcome under specified conditions.
A design that crosses levels of multiple factors to estimate main effects and interactions.
An independent biological unit, such as a donor or independently cultured sample, relevant to the inference.
F = (4/3)[E/(1 − ν²)]√R δ^(3/2); assumes a homogeneous, elastic half-space and small indentation.
Spring and dashpot in series: stress relaxes as e^(−t/τ) with τ = η/E, eventually to zero.
Instantaneous modulus E₁ + E₂, long-time modulus E₁, relaxation time η/E₂.
State method, tip geometry, depth, loading rate, location, model and fitting range.
Tuning gel stiffness can change ligand amount, tethering and porosity; measure both factors on each batch.
Main effect = average difference across the other factor; interaction = half the difference of differences.
mol/cm² × 6.022×10²³ / 10⁸ = molecules/μm²; spacing ≈ 1/√density.
Total force = traction stress × adhesive area; requires the gel modulus.
G′ = (σ₀/ε₀) cos δ (energy stored) and G″ = (σ₀/ε₀) sin δ (energy lost); tan δ = G″/G′; |G*| = √(G′² + G″²).
G′ = G(ωτ)²/(1 + (ωτ)²), G″ = G(ωτ)/(1 + (ωτ)²); the moduli cross at ω = 1/τ, where each is G/2 and δ = 45°.
E = 2(1 + ν)G, so E = 3G for ν = 0.5; always say whether a modulus is G or E.
G′ and G″ across frequency, in the culture medium at 37 °C, on an equilibrium-swollen gel, within the linear range; a single stiffness hides the relaxation.
k = 3EI/L³ = 3πEd⁴/(64L³); force F = k x for a tip deflection x; 1 N/m = 1000 nN/μm.
k ∝ d⁴/L³: doubling d gives 16 times the stiffness and halving L gives 8 times; arrays of different stiffness come from geometry.
Stress = force/area (1 nN/μm² = 1 kPa), averaged over the contact area; total force is the sum over pillars.
Beam theory needs small deflections (about 10% of L); a pillar array is a discrete set of springs, not a continuous gel, and the reference position limits the force resolution.
τ(F) = τ₀ exp(−F x_b/(k_B T)); k_B T = 4.28 pN·nm at 310 K; the lifetime halves at F = k_B T ln 2/x_b.
A bond anchored to a spring of stiffness k_s pulled at speed v loads at k_s v, so t_load = F/(k_s v); softer substrates load more slowly.
k_s* = F/(v τ(F)) equates loading time and lifetime; stiffer substrates load bonds before they fail. It depends on the assumed force, speed and bond parameters.
Many bonds, rebinding, force-dependent actin flow, catch bonds, recruitment and substrate relaxation; the clutch picture is a hypothesis to test, not a prediction.
ΔP = 2T(1/R_p − 1/R_c) for a liquid-drop cell held by a pipette; T = ΔP/(2(1/R_p − 1/R_c)), with radii, not diameters.
ΔP ∝ T; ΔP rises as the pipette narrows (1/R_p) and as the cell grows; the method needs R_p clearly below R_c.
Cortical tension (N/m) is a surface property; T/h is a stress scale, not a modulus. The cortex is not the whole cell.
Uniform surface tension, slow aspiration, a cell in suspension with a dominant cortex; adherent cells, the nucleus and viscous flow need other models.
y = y_max E^n/(EC₅₀^n + E^n); half of y_max at E = EC₅₀; inverse E = EC₅₀ (y/(y_max − y))^(1/n); slope at the midpoint n y_max/(4 EC₅₀).
Space stiffness values logarithmically across the range of interest; levels all in the saturated (or all in the flat) region can hide a large effect.
Fit to gel-level values: the gel, not the cell, is the independent unit; use enough levels (five or more) to estimate the midpoint and the steepness.
A property of a material system (ligand, viscoelasticity, assay time, marker), not of a cell type; it does not separate stiffness from properties that changed with it.
Engineering strain ε = ΔL/L₀; true strain ln(1 + ε); transverse strain −νε (ν = 0.5 for an incompressible elastomer); area strain (1 + ε)(1 + ε_t) − 1.
A 10% uniaxial stretch changes the area by about 4.5%, a 10% equibiaxial stretch by 21%; always state which.
σ = Eε and F = σA (area in m²); the strain defines the stimulus the cells follow, the force matters for the apparatus.
Peak strain rate = 2πf × amplitude; report waveform, frequency, minimum and maximum strain, duration and cycles; measure the strain in the culture area.
Average the cells within each gel, then the gel means within each condition; count gels and cells separately.
Main effect = mean over the other factor's levels of the difference; interaction = half the difference between the effects of one factor at the two levels of the other.
SE = SD(gel means) × √(2/n gels per arm); counting cells as independent understates it.
Two controlled factors do not cover viscoelasticity or ligand mobility; report them for each formulation.
VIF = 1/(1 − r²) for two correlated predictors; the standard error is inflated by √VIF (3.2 at r = 0.95); r = 1 means the effects cannot be separated.
For a circular spot of radius w, D ≈ 0.224 w²/t½; a longer recovery means a less mobile ligand; report it for each formulation.
Cross stiffness (log-spaced) with ligand density independently, add non-adhesive and scrambled-ligand controls, and characterize the moduli, density and mobility of the same gels.
SD of a gel mean = √(σ_b² + σ_w²/m); the SE of an arm difference uses gels; counting cells as independent understates it; more gels help, more cells per gel help little.
